refnamediv.refpurpose: Submit session records and evaluate trust policies

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: pam_platformd.so communicates with platformd-trustd.service8. It does not verify credentials and does not replace an authentication module.

When used as a session module with method=, it submits a record when a session is opened. The record names the PAM service, user, terminal, remote host, logind session, and declared authentication method. The module returns success regardless of submission failure.

A submitted session record is declared audit evidence. It does not establish verification freshness. Freshness is accepted only from a successful platformd-verify verification event submitted for the same logind session.
When used as an auth or account module with policy=, it evaluates the named policy. An unreachable service, a malformed or mismatched reply, and a denied policy all fail closed.

The verified-boot policy does not require a user or session. The fresh-user-verification and local-trusted-session policies require the calling process to belong to a logind session owned by the user named in PAM_USER. The module does not use XDG_SESSION_ID to select a session. Session policies fail before a session has been created, in processes outside a session, and when the PAM account differs from the session owner. Session records use the same ownership check and are omitted when it cannot be satisfied.

The module connects only to /run/platformd-trustd/io.platformd.Trust and requires a socket peer with user ID 0. Environment variables do not override this endpoint. Each exchange has a five-second deadline and requires a complete, NUL-terminated Varlink message of at most 64 KiB, including the terminator.

listitem.para: Record METHOD as the declared authentication method when a session is opened.
Evaluate POLICY for the current boot or session. Supported values are verified-boot, fresh-user-verification, and local-trusted-session. Unknown policies are denied.

refsect1.title: Return values
refsect1.para: The session module returns PAM_SUCCESS. The auth module returns PAM_SUCCESS for a satisfied policy and PAM_AUTH_ERR otherwise. The account module returns PAM_SUCCESS for a satisfied policy and PAM_PERM_DENIED otherwise. The auth and account modules return PAM_IGNORE when policy= is absent. Credential establishment returns PAM_IGNORE.

refsect1.title: Examples
refsect1.programlisting: session optional pam_platformd.so method=password auth required pam_platformd.so policy=verified-boot
